shared_context.topic: applying ointment to a pierced nipple

snippets.output: If you have a pierced nipple, applying ointment can be challenging, but it is essential to continue taking care of your nipple to prevent infection and promote healing.
snippets.pattern_notes: Challenge + reason/justification to continue care (prevent infection, promote healing) - causal/conditional linkage.

snippets.output: Gently clean the piercing area with saline solution and dry it thoroughly before applying ointment.
snippets.pattern_notes: Parallel pre-application steps: clean, then dry - enumeration of prep steps.

snippets.output: Use a clean and sterile applicator or cotton swab to apply a small amount of ointment directly to the piercing. Gently rotate the piercing to prevent the ointment from accumulating in one area, which can cause irritation.
snippets.pattern_notes: Application action + rotation step + reason (accumulation causes irritation) - causal chain.

snippets.output: Avoid tight clothing that may irritate the piercing or the ointment.
snippets.pattern_notes: Two parallel irritation targets (piercing, ointment) listed as properties of tight clothing avoidance.

snippets.output: Follow the instructions of your piercer or healthcare provider regarding ointment use and frequency of application.
snippets.pattern_notes: Enumeration of what to follow per instructions: use and frequency.

snippets.output: If you experience any signs of infection, such as redness, swelling, or discharge, you should consult your piercer or healthcare provider immediately.
snippets.pattern_notes: Recommendation (consult provider) supported by enumerated signs of infection that justify it.
